entityGroups.name: Foundations
entityGroups.description: Brand-level foundations transcribed from Imagine Cities Brand Guidelines v2.0.1 (October 2024). The guidelines are brand-level and do not document a component library, so this system documents no components.

entities.name: Colour
entities.description: The Imagine Cities palette. Gold is the hero colour. Per the guidelines, the palette is "carefully crafted for both accessibility and seamless compatibility".

metadata.summary: Seven brand colours led by Gold, plus documented tint stops.

links.label: Imagine Cities Brand Guidelines v2.0.1 (Google Slides)

items.title: Gold leads
items.description: Gold `#FFB827` is the hero colour. It carries brand recognition, so it is reserved for the elements that should be noticed first — calls to action, key icons, standout elements — rather than spread across large surfaces.

items.title: Accessible by construction
items.description: The palette was built so that its documented pairings meet contrast requirements. Pick pairings from the documented set instead of choosing colours by eye, and treat a failing pairing as a defect rather than a style choice.

items.title: Tints carry structure, not decoration
items.description: Tints exist so a page can be divided into sections without adding new hues. A 20% tint marks a section as important; it does not create a new brand colour.

items.guidance: Use Gold `#FFB827` for call-to-action buttons, key icons, and standout elements.
items.rationale: Gold is the hero colour and reserving it for primary actions keeps it legible as a signal.

items.guidance: Use Deep Azure `#0656BF` for headers, links, and secondary elements.
Use Charcoal Black `#242525` for text and Serene White `#F5F7F2` for backgrounds.
Use 20% tints of Gold, Deep Azure, or Forest Green for section backgrounds that signify important components.
items.rationale: The guidelines assign 20% tints the secondary role of marking sections without introducing further hues.

items.guidance: Restrict Bold Red `#C73124` to alerts, warnings, and emphasis of a specific area. Do not use it for calls to action, body text, or section backgrounds.
items.rationale: The guidelines direct that Bold Red be used sparingly; broad use erodes its meaning as a warning colour.

items.guidance: Use only the seven documented brand colours and their documented tint stops. Do not add hues, and do not take colours from the 2021 "Design Guidelines.pdf" (Montserrat era: Azure, Viridian, Turquoise, Aqua, gold `#F9AF42`).
items.rationale: The 2021 document is superseded; mixing its palette in corrupts the brand.

criteria.title: Large-or-bold text threshold
criteria.statement: Any pairing classified "large or bold text only" is used only at 14pt bold or larger, or 18pt regular or larger.

criteria.title: Pairings come from the documented set
criteria.statement: Every foreground/background pairing shipped in an Imagine Cities surface appears in the guidelines' pairing chart, classified either "fully compliant", or "large or bold text only" and used at or above the large-text threshold.

criteria.title: No not-compliant pairings carry text
criteria.statement: None of the four pairings classified "not compliant for texts" carries text at any size: Deep Azure with Forest Green, Bold Red with Deep Azure, Gold with Fresh Green, and Forest Green with Bold Red.

colorContrast.context: FULLY COMPLIANT — usable at any text size. Body text on the default background. Ratio 14.25:1. The pairing is symmetric: Serene White text on Charcoal Black is equally compliant.
FULLY COMPLIANT — usable at any text size. Ratio 13.34:1. Symmetric: Fresh Green on Charcoal Black is equally compliant.
FULLY COMPLIANT — usable at any text size. Label text on a Gold call-to-action surface. Ratio 8.88:1. Symmetric: Gold on Charcoal Black is equally compliant.
LARGE OR BOLD TEXT ONLY — minimum 14pt bold or 18pt regular. Ratio 6.30:1. Symmetric: Deep Azure text on Serene White, e.g. links, carries the same restriction.
LARGE OR BOLD TEXT ONLY — minimum 14pt bold or 18pt regular. Ratio 5.90:1. Symmetric.
LARGE OR BOLD TEXT ONLY — minimum 14pt bold or 18pt regular. Ratio 5.11:1. Symmetric.
LARGE OR BOLD TEXT ONLY — minimum 14pt bold or 18pt regular. Reversed text on a Bold Red alert surface. Ratio 5.00:1. Symmetric.
LARGE OR BOLD TEXT ONLY — minimum 14pt bold or 18pt regular. Ratio 4.78:1. Symmetric.
LARGE OR BOLD TEXT ONLY — minimum 14pt bold or 18pt regular. Ratio 4.68:1. Symmetric.

items.title: Tints
items.body:
Tint stops of **100 / 80 / 60 / 40 / 20%** are documented for exactly four colours — **Deep Azure, Gold, Forest Green and Bold Red**. Serene White, Charcoal Black and Fresh Green have no tint ramp. All twenty values are in `tokens/tokens.json` under `color.tint`.

| Stop | Deep Azure | Gold | Forest Green | Bold Red |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100% | `#0656BF` | `#FFB827` | `#527302` | `#C73124` |
| 80% | `#3677CA` | `#FDC550` | `#738E33` | `#D0594E` |
| 60% | `#6697D4` | `#FBD178` | `#93A862` | `#D98077` |
| 40% | `#95B6DD` | `#F9DEA1` | `#B4C292` | `#E3A89F` |
| 20% | `#C5D6E7` | `#F7EAC9` | `#D4DCC1` | `#ECCFC8` |

The ramps are mixed against **Serene White `#F5F7F2`, not pure white**. A pure-white mix drifts by up to 11 per channel at the 20% stop, so never regenerate these by formula — use the values.

**Font colour per stop**, as the chart pairs them:

| Stop | Deep Azure | Gold | Forest Green | Bold Red |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100% | Serene White | Charcoal Black | Serene White | Serene White |
| 80% | Serene White | Charcoal Black | Serene White | Serene White |
| 60% | Serene White ⚠ | Charcoal Black | Charcoal Black | Charcoal Black |
| 40% | Charcoal Black | Charcoal Black | Charcoal Black | Charcoal Black |
| 20% | Charcoal Black | Charcoal Black | Charcoal Black | Charcoal Black |

⚠ **Deep Azure 60% is a defect in the guidelines.** Serene White on `#6697D4` measures **2.80:1**, which clears no WCAG threshold — not even the 3:1 minimum for large text. Charcoal Black on the same stop measures 5.08:1. Do not ship white text on this stop; raise it with the brand owner. Every other pairing in the chart holds up.

Two more worth knowing: at Forest Green 80% and Bold Red 80% the chart picks Serene White where Charcoal Black measures marginally higher (3.45 vs 4.13, and 3.73 vs 3.82). Both clear 3:1, so both are usable for large or bold text as the chart intends.

items.title: Reading the pairing matrix
items.body:
The 2.4 slide classifies font-colour pairings as **fully compliant**, **large-or-bold text only** (minimum 14pt bold or 18pt regular), or **not compliant for texts**. It shows each pairing twice, once in each direction. Contrast is symmetric, so a classification belongs to the unordered *pair* — the `colorContrast` entries above list each pair once and say so.

Two things follow that are easy to get wrong:

- **Every fully-compliant pairing involves Charcoal Black.** Any other text colour is large-or-bold-only at best. A design that wants small text in Deep Azure, Forest Green or Bold Red has no compliant option — change the size or change the colour.
- **The deck is stricter than WCAG AA.** Its fully-compliant band starts at 7:1 (AAA for normal text), and every pairing it restricts to large-or-bold actually clears 4.5:1. Follow the deck, not the looser AA line.

Ratios shown are computed from the token hexes per WCAG 2.1 as a cross-check. They agree with the deck's classification on all thirteen pairings; where they ever disagree, the deck governs.

Pairings the slide does not show are **undocumented** — neither approved nor forbidden. Do not infer a classification for them.

documentBlocks.name: Type Scale
documentBlocks.description: The twelve documented type styles, smallest to largest. Each step names its token in `tokens/tokens.json` under `typography.*`, where the weight, line height and letter spacing live. Every value and every label-to-spec mapping is confirmed against the two "3.2 Font System" slide images. Note the hierarchy the deck defines: Headline and Subheadline are both 20px, while Subtitle is 48px.

steps.name: Title - Display
steps.description: SemiBold 72px, line height 120%, letter spacing -3%. The largest style.

entities.name: Logo
entities.description:
The logo features the Calgary Tower against a backdrop of light beams, symbolizing a future where cities thrive through the collective actions of neighbourhoods. The **Primary Logo** is the mark plus the "IMAGINE CITIES" wordmark; the **Secondary Logo** is the mark alone.

The logo is fixed artwork that sits outside the token system, and it is painted in legacy colours that are not in the v2.0.1 palette. That is intended — read the colour exception below before changing anything about it.

metadata.summary: Calgary Tower against light beams; primary and secondary variants.

items.guidance: Keep the logo's defined safe space (the clear space marked "C") free of other elements.
Do not rearrange the logo's elements.
Do not change the logo's colour or font.
Do not distort the logo, or alter its size or proportion.
Do not apply patterns or effects to the logo.
Do not rotate the logo.
Do not recolour the logo to the v2.0.1 palette. Its light beams are `#F9AF42`, `#149ED3` and `#13A89E`, and its wordmark is not Poppins — leave all of it exactly as shipped.
items.rationale: v2.0.1 kept the pre-existing logo artwork unchanged, and slide 1.2 states "Please do not change the colour or font". The legacy colours inside the logo are correct, even though `#F9AF42` is the superseded 2021 gold and appears nowhere else in the system.

items.guidance: Do not add the logo's colours to `tokens/tokens.json` or treat them as brand colours. They exist only inside the logo artwork.
items.rationale: Promoting them to tokens would reintroduce the superseded 2021 palette through the back door — the exact failure the v2.0.1-only rule exists to prevent.

items.title: Colour exception
items.body:
The logo's light beams are `#F9AF42`, `#149ED3` and `#13A89E`, sampled from the artwork. None of those is a v2.0.1 palette colour, and `#F9AF42` is specifically the **superseded 2021 gold**. The wordmark is a heavy geometric sans rather than Poppins.

This is intended. v2.0.1 kept the existing logo unchanged — slides 1.1 and 1.2 render it exactly this way, and 1.2 says "Please do not change the colour or font". The logo is fixed artwork outside the token system.

The practical consequence: seeing `#F9AF42` inside `assets/` is **not** a sign the 2021 guidelines leaked in. Seeing it in `tokens/tokens.json` would be. The two cases look alike and must be judged differently.

items.title: Assets
items.body:
| File | Source | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `assets/logos/primary-logo-black.png` | Drive `Imagine Cities Logo_black.png`, 2021-10-09 | 2551×990 RGBA | Primary Logo, black wordmark, transparent. |
| `assets/logos/primary-logo-white.png` | Drive `Imagine Cities Logo_white.png`, 2021-10-09 | 2551×990 RGBA | Primary Logo, white wordmark, transparent. For dark surfaces. |
| `assets/marks/secondary-logo.jpg` | Drive `city_diamond_large.jpg`, 2020 | 379×431 JPEG | Secondary Logo (mark alone). Low resolution, flattened white background, no transparency — a stand-in until a better file exists. |

The files date from 2020–2021 and predate the v2.0.1 deck, but the artwork is unchanged: the logo on slides 1.1 and 1.2 is this artwork.

**No vector artwork exists.** The shared Drive holds no SVG, EPS or AI file for the logo — every asset is raster, so the logo cannot currently be rendered crisply at arbitrary size. A website rebuild needs vector; request it from whoever produced the v2.0.1 deck. The Secondary Logo needs replacing too: a 379×431 JPEG with a baked white background cannot sit on any coloured surface.

The Drive folder also holds `Outside The Box Logos`, a separate sub-brand, not copied here.

Regular 20px / -2%. **The line height is a defect in the guidelines, not a transcription error** — the slide really does read 24%, confirmed against it. At 20px that is 4.8px, less than a quarter of the glyph height, so the lines would overlap and no layout can use it.

entities.name: Accessibility
entities.description: How to keep Imagine Cities work readable — colour pairings and text size.

metadata.summary: The thirteen documented colour pairings and the large-or-bold text threshold.

items.guidance: Set text at any size only in one of the three fully compliant pairings: Charcoal Black with Serene White, Charcoal Black with Fresh Green, or Charcoal Black with Gold. Either colour may be the text or the background.
items.rationale: These are the only pairings the 2.4 slide clears for unrestricted use; all three reach 7:1 or better.

items.guidance: Set text in a large-or-bold-only pairing at 14pt bold or larger, or 18pt regular or larger. Those pairings are Serene White with Deep Azure, Fresh Green with Deep Azure, Serene White with Forest Green, Serene White with Bold Red, Fresh Green with Forest Green, and Fresh Green with Bold Red.
items.rationale: The slide marks these six pairings with the 14pt-bold / 18pt-regular threshold; they land between 4.68:1 and 6.30:1.

items.guidance: Do not put text in Deep Azure on Forest Green, Bold Red on Deep Azure, Gold on Fresh Green, or Forest Green on Bold Red, at any size, in either direction.
items.rationale: The slide classifies these four pairings as not compliant for texts; they range from 1.02:1 to 1.50:1, with Forest Green on Bold Red effectively invisible.

items.guidance: Set small text in Charcoal Black. Where a design needs small text in Deep Azure, Forest Green or Bold Red, change the size or the colour rather than shipping it.
items.rationale: Every fully compliant pairing involves Charcoal Black, so no other text colour has an unrestricted option.

items.guidance: Do not set text in Serene White on the Deep Azure 60% tint `#6697D4`, at any size, even though the 2.2 chart pairs them. Use Charcoal Black on that stop instead.
items.rationale: The pairing measures 2.80:1, below the 3:1 minimum for large text and far below 4.5:1 for normal text. Charcoal Black on the same stop measures 5.08:1. This is the one chart recommendation that does not hold up when measured, and it should be raised with the brand owner.
items.evidence: Contrast computed from the deck's own tint value #6697D4 against Serene White #F5F7F2 per WCAG 2.1 relative luminance.

items.guidance: Do not classify a pairing that the 2.4 slide does not show. Undocumented pairings are neither approved nor forbidden — measure the pair and raise it with the brand owner.
Do not carry a colour pairing over from a 2021 asset. Re-check it against the v2.0.1 chart first.
items.rationale: The 2021 palette is a different set of hues, so its pairings say nothing about the current one.

items.title: The three classes at a glance
items.body:
| Class | Pairings | Ratio range |
|---|---|---|
| Fully compliant | Charcoal Black with Serene White, Fresh Green, or Gold | 8.88–14.25:1 |
| Large or bold only | Serene White with Deep Azure, Forest Green, or Bold Red; Fresh Green with Deep Azure, Forest Green, or Bold Red | 4.68–6.30:1 |
| Not compliant for texts | Deep Azure + Forest Green, Bold Red + Deep Azure, Gold + Fresh Green, Forest Green + Bold Red | 1.02–1.50:1 |

Each pairing is symmetric — either colour may be the text. The full matrix, with per-pairing ratios, is on the colour foundation.

entities.name: The Current Website (observed, not normative)
entities.description: What `www.imaginecities.com` actually does today, audited 2026-08-15. **This entity is descriptive.** The website is an implementation, not a source of brand truth — where it and v2.0.1 disagree, the deck wins and the site is what needs fixing. Nothing here may be promoted into `tokens/tokens.json`.

metadata.summary: Audit of the live site: mostly on-brand, with six defects and no spacing system to borrow.

items.title: Why this was checked
items.body:
v2.0.1 is brand-level and documents no spacing scale, no radii and no component states. The live site was audited to see whether it supplies them.

**It does not.** Padding runs across twelve ad-hoc `em` values with no common step, five different border-radius values are in use, and font sizes do not map onto the twelve documented type styles. There is no system there to extract — only inconsistency that would be laundered into legitimacy by copying it.

The full audit is in `source/observed-website.md`.

items.title: What the site gets right
items.body: Every `font-family` in the site's own CSS is Poppins. The palette is v2.0.1 — Charcoal Black (11 uses), Serene White (7), Gold (6), Deep Azure (1) — and `#D4DDC2` matches the documented Forest Green 20% tint exactly. Gold is used for calls to action, per §2.3.

items.title: The CTA pattern worth keeping
items.body:
Both button implementations render the CTA as a **pill** (`border-radius: 50px` and `2em`), which is a rounded rectangle and therefore consistent with the §4.1 holding shapes. Both hover by **inverting to Charcoal Black on Gold**, which measures 8.88:1 — a fully compliant pairing.

That is a defensible observed convention. It is still not brand-documented: if it should be normative, it belongs in the guidelines, not inferred from CSS.

items.title: Defects to fix in the revamp
items.body:
1. **Three dead font loads**, including **Montserrat** — the superseded 2021 brand font, linked from the HTML and referenced by zero CSS rules. Raleway and Noto Serif are also loaded and unused.
2. **`.learn-more-btn` sets no default text colour**, only a `:hover` colour, so the resting state falls back to the user agent link colour on Gold. Needs measuring; likely fails contrast.
3. **Weights are used but never loaded.** Poppins loads 400/500/600, but the CSS asks for `800` twice and `bold` (700) twice — those render as synthesized fakes.
4. **Button weight conflicts with the brand:** the site uses SemiBold 600 where the documented Button Text style is Medium 500.
5. **Two competing button components**, differing in padding and radius.
6. **Off-palette colours:** `#000000` (where Charcoal Black `#242525` is the brand value), `#272728`, `#E0E0E0`, `#CCCCCC`, `#C9DAF1`.

items.title: Domain
items.body: `www.imaginecities.ca`, the URL printed in the v2.0.1 deck, **does not resolve**. The live site is `www.imaginecities.com`. `systemInfo.url` records the working domain; the deck's value is preserved in `source/brand-v2.0.1.md` as transcribed.

items.guidance: Do not copy spacing, radius or font-size values from the live site into this system. They are ad-hoc and inconsistent.
items.rationale: Twelve unrelated padding values and five radii are not a scale. Codifying them would turn an implementation accident into a documented brand rule.

items.guidance: Do not treat any colour observed on the site as a brand colour unless it also appears in `tokens/tokens.json`.
items.rationale: The site carries five off-palette colours. Observation is not authority.

items.guidance: Remove the Montserrat, Raleway and Noto Serif font links from the site.
items.rationale: All three are downloaded and used by nothing. Montserrat is additionally the superseded 2021 brand font and should not be served from an Imagine Cities page.

entities.name: Using This System
entities.description: How to consume these files, and what must never enter them.

metadata.summary: Source of truth, file layout, and the v2.0.1-only rule.

items.title: Source of truth
items.body: Everything here is transcribed from **Imagine Cities Brand Guidelines v2.0.1 (October 2024)**, via `source/brand-v2.0.1.md`. Raw values live in `tokens/tokens.json` (W3C DTCG) — import that file rather than copying hexes.

items.title: What is out of scope
items.body:
The 2021 `Design Guidelines.pdf` is **superseded**: Montserrat, an Azure/Viridian/Turquoise/Aqua palette, and gold `#F9AF42`. None of it may be mixed in.

The shared Drive folder also holds a `Usernames & Passwords` document. It is out of scope for this repo and must never be ingested.

items.title: No components
items.body: The guidelines are brand-level and document no component library, so this system documents no components. Do not fabricate component specs — extend the brand foundations instead, and record any new decision back into the guidelines first.

items.guidance: Take colour and type values only from `tokens/tokens.json`. Do not hard-code hex values or type specs in downstream code.
items.rationale: A single source keeps the website, graphics and documents in sync when the brand is revised.

items.guidance: Do not add a colour, type value, or component spec that does not appear in Brand Guidelines v2.0.1.
items.rationale: Invented values become de-facto brand once they ship.
